questions.question: What does eye contact with another driver mean?

options.text: They may not yield to you properly.
They will definitely yield to you properly.

questions.correctAnswerText: They may not yield to you properly.
questions.explanation: Do not assume that eye contact means a driver will yield to you. A driver can look directly at you and still fail to see you.

questions.question: How should you swerve correctly?

options.text: Press the handgrip in the direction you want to turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip in the direction you want to turn.
questions.explanation: To swerve away from a hazard, press lightly on the handgrip on the side where you want to escape.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop completely, then go when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, then go when safe.
questions.explanation: Red octagonal signs are stop signs. You must stop completely, check for other traffic and pedestrians, and then proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slow-moving vehicle
questions.explanation: This sign appears on slow-moving vehicles traveling under 25 mph, such as farm equipment, construction vehicles, or horse-drawn wagons.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger, you will likely need to:
questions.correctAnswerText: Raise the tire pressure.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight to your motorcycle. Add a few pounds of pressure to your tires before riding. Check your owner's manual for the correct pressure.

questions.question: When riding behind another vehicle, where should you position yourself?

options.text: So the driver sees you in the side mirror.
So the driver sees you in the rearview mirror.
So the driver sees you through the passenger window.

questions.correctAnswerText: So the driver sees you in the rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Position yourself in the center of your lane behind the car. This places you in the driver's rearview mirror. Drivers check their rearview mirrors much more often than side mirrors.

questions.question: In a group ride, where should inexperienced riders be?
questions.correctAnswerText: Just behind the lead rider.
questions.explanation: Less experienced riders should ride near the front, just behind the leader. This way, experienced riders behind them can watch and help.

questions.question: The center of the lane has an oily strip. What about this strip?

options.text: It is safe to ride on unless it is raining.
Only use it when sharing a lane with another vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is safe to ride on unless it is raining.
questions.explanation: The oily center strip usually has enough traction for safe riding, except in rain. The strip is usually about two feet wide, so you can ride on either side of it and stay in the center of the lane.

questions.question: You see an emergency vehicle stopped on the side of the road with lights flashing. What should you do?

options.text: Stop behind it on the roadway.
Change lanes away from it and pass carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes away from it and pass carefully.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle, tow truck, or roadside assistance vehicle with flashing lights, change lanes to give it space. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: How should a motorcycle group pass another vehicle?
questions.correctAnswerText: One at a time
questions.explanation: On a two-lane road, motorcycles should pass one at a time. Each rider must finish passing before the next one begins.

questions.question: Changing gears while turning:

options.text: Is better than shifting before the turn.
Is the best way to control speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should only be done smoothly.
questions.explanation: It is best to change gears before you start a turn. If you must shift while turning, do it smoothly. A sudden power change to the rear wheel can cause your motorcycle to skid.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, you:

options.text: Can go 10 mph over the speed limit.
Must stay within the speed limit.
Must drive faster than the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must stay within the speed limit.
questions.explanation: Always pass other vehicles within the posted speed limit. Only pass where it is safe and legal to do so.

questions.question: Where is there the greatest risk of conflict between a motorcycle and other vehicles?
questions.correctAnswerText: At intersections.
questions.explanation: Intersections are where motorcycles and other vehicles are most likely to have problems. Riders should be extra careful when approaching intersections.

questions.question: Which statement about space between your motorcycle and other vehicles is NOT a benefit?

options.text: You have more time to react to other drivers.
You have few ways to escape.

questions.correctAnswerText: You have few ways to escape.
questions.explanation: Keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles gives you time to react and room to move safely.

questions.question: Lanes of traffic moving in the same direction are separated by:
questions.correctAnswerText: White lines.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. Solid white lines mean you cannot pass. Dashed white lines mean you can pass if it is safe.

questions.question: You should increase your following distance if:
questions.correctAnswerText: The pavement is slippery.
questions.explanation: Leave more space if your motorcycle needs longer to stop. Increase your distance if the pavement is slippery, if you cannot see ahead, or if traffic is heavy.

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks while braking on a straight road:

options.text: You must release the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can usually keep control.
questions.explanation: If your rear wheel locks while stopping in a straight line, you can keep it locked until you stop. You can usually control your motorcycle even with a locked rear wheel if it stays upright and straight.

questions.question: When it starts raining, the best place to ride is:

options.text: In the tire tracks left by other vehicles.
In the center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the tire tracks left by other vehicles.
questions.explanation: When it rains, do not ride in the center of the lane. Instead, ride in the tire tracks left by cars ahead of you. The left tire track is usually best, but this depends on traffic.

questions.question: For motorcycle riders, eye protection is:
questions.correctAnswerText: Required.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle riders must wear proper eye protection when riding.

questions.question: Convex mirrors:

options.text: Show a narrow view behind you.
Show a wide view behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Show a wide view behind you.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors show a wider view of the road behind you than flat mirrors. Objects appear farther away than they really are. Get used to your mirrors before riding.

questions.question: Your lane position should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Give you a way to escape if needed.
Show other drivers what you plan to do.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you feel wind blasts.
questions.explanation: A good lane position should help you see others and be seen. It should help you avoid wind blasts, blind spots, and road hazards. Your lane position should stop other drivers from sharing your lane and give you an escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: When looking through a turn, you should:

options.text: Turn your head only, not your shoulders.
Turn your head and shoulders to see better.
Turn your shoulders, but not your head.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head only, not your shoulders.
questions.explanation: When turning, look to where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: When it starts to rain, it is usually best to:

options.text: Ride in the center of the lane.
Pull to the side of the road and wait for the rain to stop.
Ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Roads become slippery when rain first starts, especially in the center of a lane. When it rains, it is usually safest to ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles. The left tire track is often the best choice.

questions.question: Helmets are:

options.text: Required for all motorcycle riders and passengers.
Required for all motorcycle riders and passengers under age 18.
Required for passengers, but not for riders.
Not required for anyone on a motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Required for all motorcycle riders and passengers under age 18.
questions.explanation: In Idaho, all motorcycle riders and passengers under age 18 must wear helmets. All riders and passengers should wear helmets, no matter their age.

questions.question: If carrying a load, the load should be:
questions.correctAnswerText: Secured as low as possible.
questions.explanation: If not carried in saddlebags, loads should be secured as low as possible. Attaching a load to a sissy bar can raise the motorcycle's center of gravity and affect its balance.
